texts.full_text: ST TOWN West Coast Town, the new solo album from acclaimed musician, songwriter and performer Chris Shiflett, will be released on 14th April on SideOneDummy Records. Although he’s known worldwide as the Foo Fighters’ lead guitarist, Chris’ solo country work has also made him a hit in the Alt Country scene, where his signature vocals and killer guitar work serve up a heady brew of raw barroom honky tonk, hi-octane rockabilly, and here-and-now Americana. Chris interviewed Grammy Award-winning producer Dave Cobb for his weekly podcast at Nashville’s historic RCA Studio A (shortly after Cobb moved his recording operations into the iconic room). There, amidst vintage gear and the ghosts of country music’s finest, Cobb and Shiflett formed a genuine friendship. “When I left the studio,” Chris remembers, “I thought, I have to make a record with that dude. I was already a big fan of the records Cobb produces, and his setup was just so amazing.” West Coast Town is a product of that creative partnership. Working with Dave Cobb and Grammy Award winning engineer Jason Evigan (who also worked on albums for artists such as Rihanna), Chris has crafted an album filled to the brim from start-to-finish. “I’ve always been a huge fan of West Coast music,” says Shiflett. ‘From The Doors and Led Zeppelin in their early days through Van Halen up until today with artists like Arctic Monkeys who have such clear influences on them." The potential economic consequences are far-reaching, impacting various aspects of personal finances. In terms of what led us here: Over time, Congress has enacted numerous tax cuts and spending measures without implementing corresponding revenue sources or budget adjustments to offset these decisions. This includes the Bush tax cuts from 2001 and 2003, which reduced income taxes across the board while also cutting taxes on dividends and capital gains. These policies were set with expiration dates, creating a situation where their scheduled termination would lead to substantial tax increases for many Americans if not addressed by Congress. As of now, without legislative action before January 1st, these tax cuts will expire simultaneously alongside pre-scheduled spending reductions mandated under the Budget Control Act (BCA) of 2011. The BCA was a result of negotiations during debt ceiling discussions that aimed to reduce deficits through automatic budget sequestration if an alternative deficit reduction plan wasn't agreed upon by Congress. Is there something special to do in case the Fragment is embedded in a ViewPager ? A: I hacked some code together and had a similar problem. I registered the ListView in Fragment 2 for context menu and unregistered Fragment 1. Yet somehow onContextItemSelected was never called when selecting an item from the context menu on the ListView in Fragment 2. What solved it for me was unregistering the OnContextListener of the ListView in the `onDestroyView()` method of the fragment: ```java @Override public void onDestroyView() { getListView().setAdapter(null); // clear the listview getListView().setOnItemLongClickListener(null); // remove long click listener super.onDestroyView(); } ``` I guess when you switch between fragments in a ViewPager, the previous fragment isn't destroyed immediately but instead kept for possible reuse later on. Because of this, its context menu listeners remain registered and interfere with the new fragment's listeners. By unregistering them in `onDestroyView()`, you ensure they are not active anymore once the fragment is no longer visible.

The wonderful Providence, which brought the children of Israel out of the house of bondage, was a chain of links, not one of which could be omitted without destroying the beauty, and defeating the end of the Divine economy. Had one of these links been wanting, the chain of deliverance had been defective. So, in the salvation of sinners by Jesus Christ, all the conditions, and preparatives were to the completeness, and glory of the scheme. The Son of God must consent to undertake our cause, and become our substitute—the promise must be given to Adam, and frequently repeated to the patriarchs—bloody sacrifices must be instituted, to typify the sufferings of Messiah—a line of prophets must foretell His advent, and the glory of His kingdom—He must be born in Bethlehem, crucified on Calvary, and buried in Joseph’s new tomb—must rise from the dead, ascend to the hand of the Father, and send down the Holy Spirit to guide and sanctify His Church.
